court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Aryan Kamal Wadhwa vs Biharilal Wadha (Huf) & Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Aryan Kamal Wadhwa, minor through his next friend, mother

facts_of_case: Minor filed suit for partition of HUF properties. Existence of HUF and coparceners admitted. Suit contested by defendants saying it's not bonafide.

legal_principles.principle: A minor coparcener can sue for partition and obtain a decree if his next friend shows it is for the minor's benefit.
legal_principles.held: If the Court is satisfied that the minor suing through his next friend has sued for the benefit of the minor and in the best interest of the minor, the right of partition implicit in a coparcener can be claimed by a minor coparcener also.
cited_cases: Bishundeo Narain & anr. vs. Seogeni Rai & ors., AIR (88) 1951 S.C. 280
Kakumanu Pedasubhayya & anr. vs. Kakumanu Akkamma & anr., AIR 1958 SC 1042

legal_principles.principle: There is no distinction between a major and minor coparcener in HUF as far as their rights to joint properties are concerned.
legal_principles.held: In Hindu Law there is no distinction between a major coparcener and the minor coparcener so far as their rights to joint properties are concerned. A minor is equally entitled as a major to be maintained out of the family properties and his rights to partition are 'precisely those of a major'.
cited_cases: Kakumanu Pedasubhayya & anr. vs. Kakumanu Akkamma & anr., AIR 1958 SC 1042

outcome.final_order: Court ordered partition of HUF properties by metes and bounds and delivery of plaintiff's share to him.

use_for_drafting: drafting a partition suit for a minor coparcener
advising on the rights of a minor in a HUF
guidance on delivery of share to a minor
